title: Implement a User-Defined Macro System for Repetitive Authoring Tasks
description: As Pedagogix Studio matures, curriculum authors are requesting features to improve their workflow efficiency. A common request is the ability to automate repetitive sequences of actions, such as creating a new lesson, adding a standard set of introduction and summary blocks, and setting default properties. This task involves implementing a user-facing Macro system. The agent will need to record a sequence of user commands, save them as a named macro, and allow the user to play them back on demand. This feature must be developed incrementally over several sessions, requiring the agent to retain context and build upon previous work.

project_spec.name: Pedagogix Studio – Interactive Curriculum Authoring & Simulation Suite
project_spec.description:
Pedagogix Studio is an expert-level, cross-platform desktop application written in C that empowers instructional designers and teachers to create, simulate, and distribute richly interactive lesson modules. The suite offers drag-and-drop curriculum assembly, multi-window learning analytics dashboards, and a real-time preview engine allowing educators to test behavioural state-machine driven simulations before they reach learners. Built around a strict MVC core, the project cleanly separates the educational domain model (courses, lessons, activities, assessments) from visual components (Gtk4-based workspaces, themable UI skins) and controllers that orchestrate state transitions, command routing, and event propagation.

To accommodate advanced educational workflows, Pedagogix Studio integrates a crash-reporting service, automatic update mechanism, per-user preference management, global keyboard shortcuts, and a flexible plug-in architecture that lets third-party developers add new activity types (e.g., virtual labs, coding sandboxes) or analytics providers. The application persists learning objects and session data in a local SQLite database while supporting cloud sync. Users can open multiple projects simultaneously in isolated windows, drag resources between them, and package finished lessons into shareable bundles. Every feature—from visual theme switching to file management wizards—has been engineered to serve the unique, iterative nature of instructional design.
